markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Terminal masking matches appended-MASK inference, supporting an objective-allocation experiment within BERT4Rec. (2) Feedback motivates testing prediction alignment, but cannot establish ownership, compatibility, fulfilled demand, or benefits from stronger recency weighting. (3) Geometry and margin probes describe training behavior; validation ranking requires the fixed evaluator.

**Related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already uses terminal masking, making this an incremental allocation experiment. Its paper uses sequence-normalized loss, whereas its implementation pools supervised positions; branch probability therefore need not equal objective weight. (2) [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates prediction alignment, while [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions against assuming stronger recent-history dependence helps. (3) [Gradient Surgery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782) motivates conflict diagnostics, but gradient disagreement does not establish worse HR@10.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed gap to test |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Reconstruction plus terminal masking | Branch probability versus effective coefficient allocation |
| Context dependence | Bidirectional encoding | Matched-target terminal/interior probes |
| Evidence quality | Margins and qualitative feedback | Measured ranking, uncertainty, and unsupported intent claims |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Fixed terminal allocation: 3/6/3.** Set terminal-only probability to 0.75. Originality: attributable comparison, but established objective; potential: transferable evidence, but category and loss-reduction dependence; difficulty: small sampler edit, but bookkeeping and endpoint checks matter. References: BERT4Rec, Recency Sampling.
2. **Linear terminal curriculum: 4/6/3.** Increase probability from 0.25 to 0.75. Originality: coherent combination, but familiar curriculum; potential: preserves early reconstruction, but adds schedule sensitivity; difficulty: simple schedule, but additional validation choices. Reference: [Masked History Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23649), studied in generative recommenders.
3. **Gradient-conflict diagnostic: 4/6/5.** Compare matched-target gradients. Originality: task-specific application, but standard geometry; potential: explanatory evidence, but no ranking guarantee; difficulty: one compatible model, but extra backward passes. Reference: Gradient Surgery.

### Selected experiment: fixed terminal allocation

At 10% progress, retain **p = 0.75**, provided it differs from baseline; otherwise label replication. Freeze the baseline endpoint/window sampling, random corruption, optimizer, architecture, and loss reduction. Replace each terminal target with reserved MASK; supervise only that position. Remaining examples retain baseline reconstruction.

Log actual target counts and terminal-position coverage. With pooled target averaging and mean random-branch target count m, terminal-only coefficient share is approximately **3/(3+m)**; sequence averaging gives 75% expected example weight. Neither equals gradient share. The intervention also changes target volume and endpoint repetition, limiting mechanistic attribution.

Keep one model/category, seed 42, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, fixed splits, routing, serialization, diagnostic interfaces, and left padding. Inference retains N−1 observations plus MASK and reads the final nonpadding position. Select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10. If paired host outputs exist, report a category-stratified user bootstrap interval; it excludes training variability and selection optimism. Monitor endpoint memorization without changing the evaluator.

idea.description: Prespecify terminal-only masked-supervision probability p=0.75 per training example, retaining the corrected baseline's random-masking procedure on remaining examples. Train exactly one independent BERT4Rec model per category. Interpret this as a branch-allocation intervention whose effective weighting and target volume depend on the unchanged baseline loss reduction.
idea.motivation: Terminal supervision matches appended-MASK prediction while preserving auxiliary bidirectional reconstruction. At 10% research progress, this small intervention is more attributable and affordable than a curriculum or gradient-based adaptation. It is an incremental experiment, not a new masking objective or a demonstrated solution to compatibility, ownership, stale interests, or fulfilled demand.
idea.implementation_notes:
No experimental results or baseline source code are supplied here. Before implementation, identify and record the baseline terminal probability, loss reduction, random-mask rules, eligible-history policy, endpoint/window distribution, target caps, and checkpoint-selection policy. If the baseline probability already equals 0.75, classify this condition as replication rather than silently choosing another value. Freeze these settings and change only the example-level branch probability. Do not introduce random-prefix sampling: the BERT4Rec reference generates random copies and an additional terminal example for supplied histories/windows, which differs from fresh sampled prefixes; preserve the corrected host baseline's actual policy instead.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, at most 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Use the baseline initialization, optimizer, architecture, batch size, and loss reduction. Match training limits and checkpoint-selection rules in the comparison; do not introduce validation-driven schedules. Record category-specific selected epochs and actual training time against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

For a terminal example, retain at most N items including the target, replace that final target with the reserved MASK, and store its original ID only in labels. Thus terminal training provides at most N−1 observed context items. Preserve the baseline policy for histories with fewer than two items; do not silently introduce zero-context examples or inherit an unchecked singleton assertion. Random examples retain the exact baseline corruption and supervised-position policy, including any forced masks, random replacements, or unchanged tokens. Padding contributes neither loss nor denominator. Never expose a shifted prediction target anywhere in the bidirectional input.

Document loss weighting explicitly. With pooled valid-target averaging, terminal-only examples have approximately p/[p+(1−p)m] of coefficient mass, where m is the actual expected number of supervised positions in random examples. At p=0.75 this is 3/(3+m); m=7.5 gives approximately 28.6%. This is a large-batch/aggregate approximation, not an exact expected finite-batch ratio. Report empirical per-batch coefficient shares and aggregate target counts. With per-example masked-position means followed by batch averaging, terminal examples have 75% expected coefficient weight when every example has a valid target. Random examples can also supervise their final position, so separately report total terminal-position coverage. Coefficient shares are not loss-value or gradient shares. Keep the reduction unchanged: changing it simultaneously would confound the prespecified experiment. Changes in target volume, gradient noise, and repeated endpoint exposure remain alternative explanations for any effect.

At inference, retain the latest N−1 observed items, append reserved MASK, left-pad to N, and read features at the maximum nonpadding index, never count−1. Keep the predictor writer and saved checkpoint architecture/configuration consistent. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint; do not combine independent models, checkpoints, popularity scores, or transition scores.

Retain ModelView hooks item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items), with view.model referencing the actual nn.Module. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. Keep batches shaped B×L and sampler bookkeeping exactly synchronized with the diagnosed batch. Add actual branch counts, valid-target counts, and terminal-position coverage using explicit definitions; unavailable measurements remain null. Use only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Do not infer unavailable reviews, ratings, categories, specifications, or simulator traits.

Select solely using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. If the host exposes per-user validation hit indicators for both baseline and intervention on identical fixed candidates, calculate paired differences and use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with a separately initialized reporting RNG seed 42. Within each category, resample its 200 users with replacement, use identical indices for both models, and average the four category differences equally. Report the observed difference and percentile bounds in percentage points. If paired outputs are unavailable, omit the interval rather than reconstructing candidates or changing the evaluator. The interval is conditional on fitted models, fixed candidates, datasets, and splits; it excludes training-seed, candidate-redraw, split, and category variability and does not correct repeated-selection optimism. Sampled HR@10 need not preserve full-catalog model ordering.

Higher terminal probability may repeatedly supervise a narrow endpoint distribution and encourage memorization or frequency shortcuts. Report baseline-versus-intervention training losses by branch and training-frequency/prefix-length strata where already available; these are exploratory diagnostics, not additional selection criteria. Do not claim robustness from one seed or causal resolution of qualitative feedback. Defer curricula, gradient surgery, and changes to loss normalization to separately prespecified future experiments.
idea.pseudocode:
P_TERMINAL = 0.75  # fixed before inspecting validation outcomes
baseline_spec = supplied_corrected_baseline_specification()
record(baseline_spec)
condition = 'replication' if baseline_spec.p_terminal == P_TERMINAL else 'intervention'

for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    model, optimizer = initialize_exact_baseline(category)
    for epoch in range(baseline_spec.epochs):  # <= 200
        for step in range(200):
            examples = baseline_sample_histories_or_windows()
            batch = []
            for history in examples:
                # Preserve baseline eligibility and endpoint sampling.
                if sampler_rng.random() < P_TERMINAL:
                    tokens = copy(history[-MAXLEN:])
                    labels = padding_labels_like(tokens)
                    labels[-1] = tokens[-1]
                    tokens[-1] = RESERVED_MASK
                    branch = 'terminal_only'
                else:
                    tokens, labels, corruption = baseline_random_mask(history)
                    branch = 'random_reconstruction'
                batch.append(left_pad_with_exact_bookkeeping(tokens, labels, branch))
            features = model.log2feats(batch.tokens)
            losses = baseline_per_target_losses(features, batch.labels)
            loss = exact_baseline_reduction(losses, batch.valid_targets)
            record_actual_branch_target_counts_and_coefficient_shares(batch)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        apply_exact_baseline_checkpoint_selection_policy()
    retain_one_selected_category_checkpoint()
write_predictor_with_matching_architecture_and_configuration()

# Inference for each routed category:
# tokens = left_pad(history[-(MAXLEN-1):] + [RESERVED_MASK], MAXLEN)
# index = maximum position whose token is not padding
# score real candidates using log2feats(tokens)[index]
# Host performs unchanged validation; no scores are fabricated.

# Optional reporting only, when paired host outputs are available:
# d[c,u] = hit_intervention[c,u] - hit_baseline[c,u]
# delta = mean_c(mean_u(d[c,u]))
# reporting_rng = independent_rng(seed=42)
# Repeat 10,000 times: independently resample 200 users within each category,
# compute each resampled paired mean, then average the four means equally.
# Report 100*delta and 100*percentile(replicates, [2.5, 97.5]).

originality.positive: A prespecified comparison with explicit loss-allocation accounting provides useful task-specific evidence.
originality.negative: Terminal masking is established BERT4Rec practice; changing its branch probability is incremental.

future_potential.positive: An interpretable result can guide later objective normalization, curricula, and matched-target diagnostics.
future_potential.negative: The intervention jointly changes target volume and endpoint exposure, and one fixed-seed benchmark comparison offers limited evidence of transfer.

code_difficulty.positive: The training intervention is principally an existing sampler probability change and preserves the backbone.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducibility requires auditing loss reduction, endpoint sampling, singleton handling, bookkeeping, and predictor consistency.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Includes terminal masking and appended-MASK inference.
Equation 8 normalizes the masked-target loss within each sequence, highlighting the distinction between example allocation and position allocation.
limitations: Terminal masking itself is prior work.
The paper does not establish an optimal terminal-example probability for these four datasets or specify fresh random-prefix sampling.
The paper's sequence-normalized presentation differs from the reference implementation's pooled valid-target reduction.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference implementation: training loss
contributions: Pools supervised-position losses and divides by valid-target weight, excluding padding targets.
Makes explicit why examples with more masked targets can contribute more total coefficient weight.
limitations: The corrected host baseline must be checked directly; reference behavior cannot be assumed.
Coefficient allocation does not determine actual loss-value or gradient allocation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec reference implementation: example generation
contributions: Generates random masked copies and terminal-only examples from supplied histories or overlapping windows.
Replaces the terminal target with MASK and retains its original item ID as the label.
Exposes endpoint repetition, context-length limits, and singleton-handling details relevant to reproducibility.
limitations: Reference defaults and stale corruption comments should not substitute for auditing the supplied baseline.
Repeated window endpoints differ from fresh prefix sampling, and singleton terminal examples can fail an assertion.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling
contributions: Motivates examining alignment between training supervision and future-item recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish that p=0.75 improves the supplied baseline.
Terminal supervision allocation is distinct from imposing stronger recency weighting on history.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Motivates examining whether recent-history dependence becomes excessive.
limitations: Does not directly evaluate the proposed terminal-mask allocation experiment.

related_work.title: Masked History Learning
contributions: Motivates shifting emphasis from history reconstruction toward prediction during training.
limitations: The supplied evidence concerns generative recommenders; transfer to BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis.
A curriculum introduces additional choices that weaken attribution in this initial experiment.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Provides a basis for examining conflicting gradients between objectives.
limitations: Negative gradient agreement is a local diagnostic rather than proof of worse validation ranking.
Matched terminal/interior BERT4Rec gradient comparisons are a proposed application and require extra computation.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling, supporting shared user indices for model comparisons.
limitations: Category-stratified macro resampling requires preserving the task's four-category aggregation.
Ordinary bootstrap intervals do not correct validation-selection optimism or measure training-seed variability.

related_work.title: R boot documentation
contributions: Documents stratified resampling, supporting independent user resampling within each category.
limitations: The proposed interval assumes independent users within categories and remains conditional on fixed benchmark inputs.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled recommendation metrics and their relationship to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator.
Bootstrapping fixed sampled candidates cannot remove discrepancies between sampled and full-catalog model ordering.
